one_line_contribution: The first controlled measurement of contamination harm in an agent experience bank as a function of writer-reader policy proximity (own policy > same-backbone variant > foreign backbone), paired with a judge x writer detection table claiming a model is least able to flag masked failures written by its own backbone and that a foreign judge's filter recovers harm the reader's own judgment cannot.
closest_prior_work: Verified threat: arXiv:2606.24428 'Escaping the Self-Confirmation Trap: An Execute-Distill-Verify Paradigm for Agentic Experience Learning' (2026-06-23, s2, 1 citation, verified via s2cli paper) already frames self-written experience as a self-confirmation problem and already prescribes the proposal's remedy - heterogeneous (foreign) agents verifying experience before it enters the bank - as a working method. It does not, as far as its abstract goes, manipulate writer identity at fixed content, measure harm-versus-proximity, or produce a judge x writer recall table, so P1/P2 survive; but P5's 'a foreign judge's filter beats the reader's own' is close to a published recipe, and an AC will read the proposal as measuring why EDV works rather than as a new claim. Second threat, verified: the detection half is a transplant of an established effect. arXiv:2404.13076 'LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations', arXiv:2410.21819 'Self-Preference Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge' (bias tracks familiarity/perplexity of the text, which is exactly the proposal's mechanism), arXiv:2507.02778 'Self-Correction Bench: the Self-Correction Blind Spot', arXiv:2607.09803 (a formal/spectral model of that blind spot), arXiv:2608.18091 (self- vs other-labels induce bidirectional judge bias) and arXiv:2512.02304 'When Does Verification Pay Off?' (solver-verifier systems work better across model families) together predict P3, P4 and the offline half of P5 before any experiment is run. Not one of these appears in the proposal's Related Work or its collision check, even though its own title word is 'blind spot'. Also close, same environment: arXiv:2605.29463 'Honest Lying: Understanding Memory Confabulation in Reflexive Agents' (2026-05, verified) shows on ALFWorld that self-generated reflective memory stores confident false task interpretations that persist across resets, and that replacing self-diagnosis with programmatic extraction fixes it - the harm-from-your-own-memory claim in the proposal's own environment, without the writer-identity manipulation. Note on the proposal's own citations: I verified 2512.16962, 2607.10608, 2605.23723, 2603.02240, 2608.10509, 2602.00428, 2605.22842, 2310.14814 and 2403.03095 by id; arXiv:2606.30566 ('forensic trajectory signatures'), cited in Related Work, does NOT resolve on either channel and I could not verify it exists.
strongest_objection: The contaminant sets are matched on type, length and a coarse coherence filter, but not on how wrong the failure is - and that, not writer proximity, is the likeliest driver of the harm ordering. Each writer's failure pool is conditioned on that writer's own success rate: Q-self fails on 47% of its training games and contributes many near-misses (correct procedure, wrong final receptacle); gpt-oss-120b 'fails rarely' and therefore contributes only catastrophic failures; EXAONE sits somewhere between. Type-matching within pick/heat/cool does not equalise the residual procedure correctness of the trajectory, and a masked near-miss and a masked disaster are different contaminants regardless of who wrote them. Worse for the headline, the two are anti-correlated with proximity in a way that can produce D_Q >= 5 with no proximity mechanism at all: the closest writer supplies the most plausible-looking, most executable, most nearly-correct wrong procedures, which is a content property that would survive a change of author. The proposal's separation of proximity from backbone (Q-prox-T/S) does not touch this, because raising temperature or swapping the ReAct template also changes what the failures look like; the manipulation check only gates pi and k=0 success, not failure quality. There is no arm in which the same failed action sequence is re-authored by a different writer, so 'written by my policy' is never separated from 'the actions my policy would have produced' or from 'this failure was closer to correct'. A reviewer will say the design measures a property of each writer's failure distribution and labels it proximity. The second-order version of the same objection: the confirmatory margins are arithmetically hard because they are bounded by total harm - D_Q >= 5 net requires E-self to be nearly harmless if Gate 0 lands near its 6-net floor, and R(cross) >= 6 net requires near-complete removal at that same floor (the entailment check flags this) - so the modal outcome of this expensive plan is a page of intervals reported as underpowered.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Add a re-authoring cross-over arm: take Q-self's masked failed trajectories and have E re-emit them in its own voice with the action content held fixed, and vice versa (verified by action-sequence equality, only surface form allowed to change), then run both. Harm that follows the actions rather than the author kills the proximity account cleanly; harm that follows the author is the paper. This is the arm that turns a correlational writer contrast into the claimed mechanism, and it is cheap relative to the 28,496 episodes already planned. (2) Match contaminants across writers on a measured wrongness score - fraction of the reference walkthrough achieved, or first divergent step - and report harm within wrongness stratum, not only within type and length. (3) Calibrate each judge's 5% false-rejection operating point per writer column on that writer's clean successes (collect clean items for every writer, not only for Q), and report the diagonal deficit net of the clean-item self-preference gap; as written, the operating point is set on clean expert items only, so the deficit measures style familiarity - the already-published self-preference effect - as much as failure blindness. (4) Run the mirror filter cells (own vs cross judge on the E-self bank) so P5 is not a statement that E is simply the better judge. (5) Express P5's recovery as a fraction of realised harm(Q-self), as rho_c already is, instead of a fixed 6 net. (6) Rewrite Related Work against the self-preference / self-correction-blind-spot literature and against 2606.24428, and state what the proposal adds beyond them - most defensibly: proximity as a graded axis, and the harm side, which none of them measures. (7) Drop or demote P4: at a paired half-width of ~0.063 its stated falsifier requires a negative point estimate in both judges at once, so it cannot fail in practice at 600 items per writer.
missing_baseline: Two. First, the symmetric filter arm: the own-judgment vs cross-judge filter cells are run only on the Q-self bank, so 'the foreign judge's filter recovers more' is confounded with 'E is a better judge of everything'. The interaction covariate protects the offline detection table but not the two downstream filter cells that P5 actually rests on; the missing cells are filter-by-Q and filter-by-E applied to the E-self bank (reader Q), which is the only way the foreignness of the judge is separated from its quality. Second, and cheaper than any judge: a provenance-only filter that drops every self-written item without reading it. The proposal's stated payoff is that 'writer identity, not just content, is a required field for any read-time filter' - the baseline for that claim is filtering on the field alone, which costs zero inference and, if the headline P1 is true, removes exactly the worst contaminants. If the foreign-judge filter does not beat the provenance filter, the detection half of the paper has no practical consequence. (A third, minor: the terminal-line regex is reported for scale, but no length- or perplexity-based cheap detector is run, and the self-preference literature says perplexity is the operative variable.)
preprint_collision: No verified collision on the central claim - no paper I found measures contamination harm as a function of writer-reader proximity with a reader swap. But the proposal's own check is thin in the one direction that matters, and I found threats it missed. Queries I ran, all through the literature command (s2cli.py, S2 + HF, both 'ok'; WebSearch unavailable on this node, WebFetch not used): (1) 'self-preference bias LLM judge fails to detect its own errors self-generated text' -> 2404.13076, 2410.21819, 2507.02778, 2406.07791, 2402.11436, 2506.02592 - the documented home literature of P3/P4, entirely absent from the proposal. (2) recent: 'agent experience memory contaminated by its own failed trajectories writer identity harm reader detection' -> 2606.24428 (EDV), 2605.29463 (Honest Lying, ALFWorld), 2607.10608, 2607.06595, 2512.16962, 2510.02373. (3) verification by id of 2606.24428, 2605.29463, 2607.10608, 2512.16962 -> all four exist as described. (4) verification by id of the proposal's Related Work: 2605.23723, 2603.02240, 2608.10509, 2602.00428, 2605.22842, 2310.14814, 2403.03095 all verified; 2606.30566 NOT FOUND on either channel - the proposal cites it as forensic trajectory signatures and I could not verify it. (5) recent: 'heterogeneous cross-model verifier filters self-generated experience before storing agent memory self-confirmation' -> 2606.24428 again, plus 2606.25161 (TRUSTMEM). (6) recent: 'model detects errors in another model's output better than in its own generations cross-model verification asymmetry' -> 2512.02304 (verification pays off more across model families), 2605.02915, 2604.22271. (7) 'conflicting retrieved memory trajectory-level diagnosis enter propagation recovery' -> 2607.10608 (the proposal's closest named method, confirmed as it describes it), 2605.28009 MemGuard, 2607.01071. (8) recent: 'relabelled failed trajectories as successful demonstrations ALFWorld experience replay harms agent success rate' -> nothing that plants relabelled failures by writer; 2605.29463 is the nearest. Judgement of the proposal's check: it searched the adversarial-memory-poisoning vocabulary and the pseudo-labeling confirmation-bias vocabulary competently and verified 2607.10608 by id, which is more than most submissions do. It did not search the vocabulary of its own headline - self-preference, self-recognition, self-correction blind spot, cross-family verification - where the detection half of the contribution is already published, and it missed 2606.24428, which is the closest published form of its cross-judge remedy and appeared under two different queries of mine. An unsearched home vocabulary is a weakness, and here it changes the novelty score: the harm half is new, the detection half is a transplant.
